skill.name: image

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, documentation links, visual-design terms, and recommendations to capture real screenshots instead of generating fake interfaces. One shell example runs local image tools, and its curl command performs an outbound request. The prompting guide also recommends third-party uploads of product and brand assets without privacy safeguards.

remediation.issue: The guide recommends uploading product screenshots and brand assets to an external image service.
remediation.suggestion: Require user approval and advise removing confidential data before upload. Tell users to review provider storage, training, and retention terms.

remediation.issue: The optimization block includes commands that modify wildcard-matched image files.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to back up files, preview matched paths, and run commands on copies before batch processing.

remediation.issue: The page inspection example performs an outbound curl request to a user-supplied site.
remediation.suggestion: Require an approved public HTTP or HTTPS URL. Warn against internal, authenticated, or sensitive endpoints.

content.value_statement: Marketing teams need consistent images that fit each channel and load quickly. This skill plans generation, design, resizing, screenshots, and web optimization.
actual_capabilities: Recommends image models or design tools based on the asset type, brand needs, text requirements, and production volume.
Turns a marketing brief into a structured image prompt covering subject, setting, style, lighting, composition, and dimensions.
Provides dimensions and aspect ratios for common blog, social, profile, marketplace, and app listing placements.
Plans product mockups that preserve real interface details through screenshots, device frames, labels, and overlays.
Recommends WebP, AVIF, JPEG, PNG, or SVG formats with resizing, compression, lazy loading, and accessibility guidance.
Explains static and dynamic OG image workflows, required metadata, reusable templates, and delivery options.
limitations: A compatible image service or design tool is required to produce final visual files.
Generated text, logos, interface details, and brand consistency still require human review.
Model features, prices, platform dimensions, and browser support can change after publication.
Real product screenshots, logos, fonts, and private brand assets must come from the user.

use_cases.title: Produce Blog and Social Visuals
use_cases.description: Create structured concepts, prompts, dimensions, and export plans for articles and organic social campaigns.

use_cases.title: Build Product Launch Galleries
use_cases.description: Turn real interface screenshots into branded mockups, marketplace galleries, profile banners, and feature announcements.

use_cases.title: Improve Web Image Delivery
use_cases.description: Choose formats, compression settings, responsive delivery patterns, and dynamic OG workflows for faster pages.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Blog Hero
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 1200x630 blog hero for [topic]. Propose one visual concept, choose an image model, and write a structured generation prompt.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for a single article image with no established creative direction.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt a Social Campaign
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan social graphics for [campaign] on [platforms]. Give exact dimensions, a reusable visual direction, crop guidance, and export recommendations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when one campaign needs consistent assets across several social platforms.

prompt_templates.title: Design Product Screenshot Mockups
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a product launch gallery using my approved screenshots and brand assets. Preserve interface details, recommend frames, and specify annotations for each image.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for product listings, feature launches, or sales materials that must show the real interface.

prompt_templates.title: Automate Dynamic OG Images
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an automated OG image workflow for [site stack] and [content source]. Define a branded template, dynamic fields, metadata, optimization, and validation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for advanced publishing systems that need unique preview images at scale.

output_examples.input: Create a hero image plan for an article about email deliverability.
output: Concept: A bright message signal passing through layered filters toward a clear inbox.
Format: 1200x630 WebP under 200 KB, with a JPEG fallback.
Tool: Flux or Gemini for the first draft, followed by brand review.

output_examples.input: Plan a Twitter/X company header that shows our product and tagline.
output: Canvas: 1500x500 with critical content centered away from avatar overlap.
Composition: Brand color field, short tagline, and one approved product screenshot.
Workflow: Build in Figma or Canva, then review at actual display size.

output_examples.input: Recommend a web delivery plan for a large product photograph.
output: Primary format: WebP at the rendered dimensions and approximately 80 percent quality.
Fallback: JPEG for clients without the preferred format.
Delivery: Responsive sources, explicit dimensions, lazy loading below the fold, and descriptive alt text.

best_practices: Provide the placement, dimensions, brand assets, visual style, and required text before choosing a production method.
Use approved real screenshots for product interfaces and review every asset for confidential or personal information.
Test readability, cropping, file size, metadata, and visual consistency at each final display size.
anti_patterns: Do not ask image models to invent real product interfaces, exact logos, or long paragraphs of text.
Do not upload private screenshots or brand assets to external services without approval and data review.
Do not publish oversized images without compression, responsive sizing, explicit dimensions, and suitable fallback formats.

faq.question: Does this skill generate image files by itself?
faq.answer: It provides plans and prompts. Final generation requires an available image model, API, or design tool.

faq.question: Which image model should I use?
faq.answer: The choice depends on photorealism, text accuracy, editing needs, brand consistency, volume, budget, and available tools.

faq.question: Can it create accurate product screenshots?
faq.answer: No image model reliably reproduces a real interface. Capture approved screenshots and use the skill to plan framing and annotations.

faq.question: What format should I use for website images?
faq.answer: WebP is the general default. Consider AVIF for smaller files, JPEG fallbacks, PNG for lossless screenshots, and SVG for vectors.

faq.question: Can it prepare assets for several social platforms?
faq.answer: Yes. It can list platform dimensions, recommend a master composition, and plan crops or template variants.

faq.question: How should private brand assets be handled?
faq.answer: Remove confidential data, obtain approval, and review each provider's storage, training, and retention terms before uploading assets.
